gaps.sentence: The invitation ___ (send) to the wrong address — nobody on this street received one.
gaps.explanation: Perfect modal passive: must have been + sent. The evidence forces the conclusion.

gaps.sentence: The passengers ___ to fasten their seatbelts as the plane entered the storm.
gaps.explanation: 'The passengers were told to …' — passive of 'tell somebody to do'.

gaps.sentence: Your name ___ (find) anywhere on the guest list, I'm afraid.
gaps.explanation: Modal passive of ability/possibility: cannot be + past participle.

gaps.sentence: The results ___ (EXPECT) to be announced later today.
gaps.explanation: 'Later today' requires the present: are expected to be announced.

gaps.sentence: Construction ___ (halt) after the discovery of Roman remains.
gaps.explanation: Past simple passive: was + halted. The halting authority is unnamed.
'She hates' takes a gerund; the passive gerund is 'being watched'.

gaps.sentence: My laptop ___ (service) next week, so back up your files beforehand.
gaps.explanation: 'Next week' takes the future passive: will be + serviced (is being serviced is also a valid arrangement).

gaps.sentence: The winners ___ a trophy at the closing ceremony.
gaps.hint: passive of a verb with two objects
gaps.explanation: Give somebody something → somebody is given something: future passive will be + given.
